correctness.rationale: The proof reduces zero defense to W-f(v*) and totality to support meeting at least two partner pairs. For W>=4 defense is automatic. The generating-function subtraction counts every support contained in at most one pair exactly once, and the only surviving invalid labelings have weights two and three with counts 2n(n-1) and 4n(n-1). All weight-three all-one labelings are feasible, yielding the complete minimum family. An exhaustive checker agrees coefficientwise for n=2 through 5.

value.rationale: Cocktail party graphs are a standard complement-of-perfect-matching family and a natural balanced complete multipartite benchmark. The result resolves the entire feasible-function weight distribution, not merely a known scalar parameter. The structural threshold at weight four explains the closed polynomial, while the corollaries give an exact total count and complete minimum-function family.
